summary_paragraph: A woman with AIDS (CD4 6, off antiretroviral therapy) and end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis presented from dialysis with acute worsening of chronic right-sided facial/forehead pain related to prior herpes zoster ophthalmicus, along with dizziness and hypotension. In the ED she received IV fluids and was initially treated empirically with vancomycin/cefepime and acyclovir due to concern for possible infection or zoster reactivation; head CT and chest X-ray showed no acute process. She had a transient episode of atrial fibrillation during resuscitation that reverted to sinus rhythm and was managed with aspirin. With stabilization of blood pressure near her baseline and no evidence of infection, antibiotics were stopped; adrenal insufficiency was evaluated with cortisol testing and a stimulation test that was not consistent with adrenal disease. Ophthalmology found no acute ocular concern. Symptoms were managed with fexofenadine for pruritus/rash felt consistent with HIV-associated eosinophilic folliculitis/prurigo and amitriptyline for post-herpetic neuralgia; she continued hemodialysis (with transient intradialytic hypotension responsive to a small saline bolus) and her renal medications. Given very low CD4 count, opportunistic infection prophylaxis with TMP-SMX and azithromycin was restarted, and she was discharged home with follow-up plans and continuation of dialysis.
